answer: Grading panels are chosen by stake-weighted sortition from an unpredictable per-epoch seed, so nobody knows which jurors will judge an answer until the draw lands, about as callable as a comet's next return. A sybil cannot steer its clones onto a chosen panel; to reliably control one it must own a large fraction of all established stake, not pile up cheap identities like scrap timber. The honest majority verdict stays the trust signal, and forging it costs real locked capital per unit of influence, not mere duplication.
